data.summary: The truck is operating within nominal electro‑thermal limits but is showing early signs of thermal stress in the motor and approaching the mid‑point of its projected cycle life. SOH remains at the commissioning baseline (78.7%), indicating no measurable capacity loss yet, but the remaining useful life (≈1245 cycles) is being consumed (448 cycles used). The current pack voltage (74.4 V) and SOC (55 %) are acceptable, yet the motor temperature (51 °C) is trending upward under load, prompting the system‑generated WARNING.
data.why_performing_this_way: Electro‑thermal: Continuous discharge at ~‑16 A while traveling at 50 km/h raises motor temperature to 51 °C; the controller is also warm (43.5 °C). LFP chemistry tolerates high temperatures, but sustained motor heat accelerates internal resistance growth. Cycle aging: 448 equivalent full cycles have been logged, representing ~36 % of the predicted 1245‑cycle RUL, so the pack is entering the mid‑life regime where subtle impedance rise begins. Behavioral: The driver’s relatively aggressive speed‑to‑load ratio and frequent shallow‑to‑moderate discharges keep the pack in the 30‑60 % SOC window, which is optimal for LFP but combined with motor heat creates a thermal‑aging feedback loop.
root_causes: Sustained motor load causing elevated motor temperature
Cumulative cycle count approaching mid‑life of the pack
Ambient/operational conditions leading to modest controller heating
Current discharge rate (‑16 A) near the upper end of typical duty for a 12.4 kWh LFP pack
prescriptive_actions: Schedule a motor and controller thermal inspection at the next service window; verify cooling fan operation and thermal interface integrity.
Implement a driver advisory to limit sustained speeds above 45 km/h when the pack SOC is between 30‑70 % to reduce motor heat buildup.
Add a 5 % buffer to minimum SOC (avoid dropping below 25 %) during trips to keep pack voltage above 70 V and reduce stress on the LFP cells.
Plan a preventive pack re‑balancing and impedance check after the next 200 cycles (≈≈800 total cycles) to catch early resistance growth.
Update the fleet telematics alert thresholds: motor temperature warning at 55 °C, controller warning at 45 °C, and schedule a maintenance ticket if either is exceeded.
